surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Rinzel ends it in overtime
paras: Dillon Boucher and Adam Klapka opened the game with a fight, and Ryan Strome opened the scoring for the Flames midway through the first. It was a busy second period. Roman Kantserov and Ryan Donato scored less than two minutes apart early in the period to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead. Patrick Kane pushed the lead to 3-1 on the power play a minute and a half later. Jonathan Castagna pulled the Flames within one midway through the second. The Flames’ Martin Pospíšil left late in the period and didn’t return. Two days later, he was ruled out with an upper-body injury. The Blackhawks’ Anton Frondell left after the second period and didn’t return. Two days later, he was listed as day to day. Yegor Sharangovich tied it 3-3 for Calgary on the power play early in the third. Chicago had what would have been the winner taken off for offside in overtime, but it didn’t cost them in the end. Sam Rinzel won it with 15 seconds left in overtime. Kane and Rinzel each had a goal and two assists.
The Flames had a little more of the play, but the Blackhawks had the finish. Spencer Knight made 33 saves for the Hawks, and Dustin Wolf stopped 29 of 33 at the other end.

Wyatt Kaiser was thrown out with a match penalty late in the second. The Blackhawks improved to 7-14-2, still last in the Central, while the Flames dropped to 10-12-2 but climbed to fifth in the Pacific.

items.text: It was the Blackhawks’ first road win of the season, in their tenth road game.
Sam Rinzel has a point in five straight games.
With Connor Bedard out, Donato took his spot and scored.
Patrick Kane scored for the first time in 18 games.
